(Alexander Pope's English)
Stranger, or friend? On these shores it is hard to know which until the meal is eaten.
Be kind to a wanderer, friend. Zeus watches over strangers and beggars.
Welcome, stranger. Come in out of the sun; you shall eat first, and then tell us what you need.
Another stranger with news of my husband? Every one of them has had news. None of it was true.
Do not be afraid. I have been beside you longer than you know.
Come, son of Odysseus. A ship and a crew are ready, and the wind with them.
Mentes, king of the Taphians
Greetings, young man. I am an old friend of your father's house.
Eurycleia, the old nurse
Mind the bad maids, child. And keep away from the suitors' end of the hall.
Eumaeus, the swineherd
Down, dogs! Come in, old man, come in; the dogs nearly had you. Sit, and eat.
Philoetius, the cowherd
Good day to you, stranger. You put me in mind of my master. He too may be wandering in rags.
Melanthius, the goatherd
Out of my way, beggar. The suitors want their goats.
Another beggar at the feast? Take your scraps and go.
The queen will choose soon. She must. And it will be me.
Good health to you, old father. May better days come to you.
They make me sing for them. I sing; what else can a bard do?
I hear what the suitors plot. I tell the queen.
I dig my vines and wait. My son will not come home. Twenty years.
Argos, the old hound
Welcome, strangers. Share in the sacrifice to Poseidon first; then you shall tell us who you are.
Peisistratus, son of Nestor
I'll drive you to Sparta myself, son of Odysseus. The horses are ready.
Welcome, both of you! Eat first; then tell me whose sons you are.
Who is this young man? He has the very look of Odysseus.
Stay a while, wanderer. The island is quiet, and the wine is sweet.
Zeus sends me. I would not have chosen the long way across all that salt water myself.
Stranger, you do not seem a bad man or a fool. Come, I will show you the way to the city.
Alcinous, king of the Phaeacians
Welcome to our hall, stranger. Here no guest goes away unhappy.
Arete, queen of the Phaeacians
Where do you come from, stranger, and who gave you those clothes?
Demodocus, the blind bard
Sit by me, friend. What song would you hear?
Laodamas, son of Alcinous
Will you try the games, stranger? You have the build of a fighter.
You look more like a trader than an athlete.
Aeolus, keeper of the winds
Tell me of Troy, guest. Tell it all. The winds can wait.
Come in, come in. Sit. Drink. You must be weary.
I don't like it. I don't like any of it.
Is it morning already?
Stand back from the blood, and let me drink, and I will tell you the truth.
Anticleia, mother of Odysseus
My child, how did you come down here, alive, into the dark?
The shade of Achilles
Do not try to comfort me about death.
The shade of Agamemnon
Odysseus! Hear how I came home.
Who are you? Where is your ship?
Lampetie, daughter of the Sun
These are my father's cattle. They are never born and they never die.
Master! Is it you? It is you!
Eupeithes, father of Antinous
My son is dead. Someone will answer for it.
Halitherses, the old prophet
I watch the birds, and the birds speak plainly.
Theoclymenus, the seer
I am a seer, fleeing a death in Argos. Take me aboard, son of Odysseus.
Get off my doorstep, old man, or I'll drag you off it by the foot!
Eurynome, the housekeeper
The queen is in her room. I'll tell her you're here.
Two young lords on the road at nightfall! Stay the night under my roof.

A fisherman with his catch
Bream and red mullet, fresh from the bay!
A woman with a water jar
The fountain's running sweet this year.
An old man in the sun
I remember when King Odysseus sailed. Twenty years. Twenty.
A girl with a basket of figs
Figs from the terraces! Taste one.
A boy chasing a hoop
Have you seen my dog?
Good clay on this island, if nothing else.
The suitors eat and eat up at the house. Shameful.
Goat cheese, stranger? Better than the suitors deserve.
Pine for the hull, fir for the oars, and pray to Poseidon.
A trader from Taphos
Iron for copper, friend. Always a fair trade.
A sailor coiling rope
Wind's from the north. Good for the mainland.
The sea gives, the sea takes.
The goats go up Neriton at dawn and come down at dusk.
A woman picking olives
Beat the branches gently, or the tree remembers.

Ten years of war and Nestor came home safe. The gods love that old man.
Pylian horses! Nothing faster from here to Argos.
A boy with a goose
Have you seen the king? He's a hundred, they say.
Mind the jars, stranger.
I was at Troy with Nestor. Ninety ships we took.
The sea's calm for you, friend. Poseidon is pleased with us.

Helen is home, and the king. They say she weaves violet wool now, as if nothing ever happened.
A farmer with a mule
Rain's coming off Taygetus. Look at it.
A girl with a goose
Two weddings at the king's house today!
Menelaus brought back horses from Egypt. You should see them run.
Eight years he wandered after Troy, the king. Eight.
The flocks go up the mountain when it's hot.
Purple from the sea, wool from the hills.

A nymph of the springs
The water runs four ways here, and every way is sweet.
A nymph with a basket of grapes
Take some. The vines never stop.
A nymph at the loom
Our mistress weaves with a golden shuttle. We only wind the wool.
A nymph of the wood
He sits on the headland every day. Every single day.

A Phaeacian shipwright
Our ships need no steersman: they know the thoughts of men, and go where we wish.
Twist it tight, it holds a ship in a storm.
Our women weave as well as our men sail. Athena taught us.
Can you dance? Everyone here can dance.
An old sea-captain
We take anyone home, stranger. Anyone, anywhere.
A girl with a basket of pears
From the king's orchard. It never stops fruiting.
A ship's carpenter
Pine for the oars. Always pine.
The world comes to Scheria for our ships.

A Ciconian woman at her door
Ships on the beach! Run and tell the men inland, the ones who fight from chariots.
A Ciconian spearman
Our brothers inland fight from horseback, and on foot if they must.
Maron's wine is so strong you mix one cup with twenty of water.
Troy's allies, we were. Much good it did us.
Apollo's priest lives in the grove. No one touches him.
the beach of the Lotus-Eaters
the village of the Lotus-Eaters
A Lotus-Eater, smiling
Sit down. Eat. Why would you ever go anywhere?
A Lotus-Eater woman
Honey-sweet, the fruit. Try one. Only one.
Home? I had one once, I think.
A girl with lotus flowers
They never fight here. They never want anything.
A sailor who stayed
My ship left. I don't mind. I don't mind anything.

Into the cave of the Cyclops
One of Odysseus' crew
Goats on that island, captain, thousands of them, and no one to hunt them.
Smoke up there on the mountain. And bleating. Big bleating.
The ship's helmsman
Twelve ships on the goat island. We came over with just ours.

Six of us, six sisters. We feast every day in our father's hall.
A daughter of Aeolus
The winds? Father keeps them. Zeus gave him the keeping.
A steward of Aeolus
The island floats, you know. Some mornings it is somewhere else.
A son of Aeolus, younger
Hear that? That's the wind in the wall.

the high house of Antiphates
The captain moored us out here on the point. He doesn't like harbours he can't see out of.
Smoke inland. No ploughing, no cattle-work. Strange country.
Here the herdsman going out calls to the one coming in. Day and night run together.

A handmaid of Circe, a nymph of the springs
Our mistress sings at her loom. Go in, if you dare.
A handmaid of Circe, a nymph of the groves
Wash first. Then wine. That is how she welcomes guests.
A handmaid of Circe, a nymph of the sacred rivers
She has a herb for everything. Everything.
A handmaid of Circe
The wolves won't hurt you. Not any more.

One of Odysseus' crew, shivering
The sun never comes here. Never.
Mist on the water, mist on the land. I want to go home.
A young oarsman, praying
Persephone's poplars. Don't touch them.
into Erebos, the House of Hades (its own door in the Hall of Doors)

🌑 The road on down Past this rock, where the dark rivers fall together, the way goes on down into Erebos, the House of Hades, with all its halls and fields of the dead. It has its own door in the Hall of Doors.
the headland facing the Sirens' isles
the Sirens' flowering meadow
Come here, famous Odysseus, glory of the Greeks. Stop your ship and listen.
No one ever sailed past without hearing our sweet voices. We know everything.
A fisherman on the headland
No one sails close to those islands. No one comes back.
Listen. Can you hear singing?
Wax in your ears, they say. Or rope.
the Sicilian shore of the strait
the wild fig tree over Charybdis
A Sicilian fisherman
Three times a day she drinks the sea, three times she spits it out. Keep to the other side.
The other side has worse. Six heads. Six.
Better to lose six men than the whole ship. That is the sum of it.
the beach of Thrinacia
the hollow sea-cave where the nymphs dance
the meadows of the Sun's cattle
the hill above the meadows
Phaethusa, daughter of the Sun
My sister and I keep our father's herds. He sees everything, stranger. Everything.
One of Odysseus' crew, hungry
A month of south wind. A month! And all that beef on the hoof.
A sailor with a fishing line
Fish, birds, whatever the hand can catch. Not the cattle. Not the cattle.
Another of the crew
Eurylochus says we'd be better drowned than starved.
